No. The per-controller plan is not ready to hand to Fable as a whole: business rules must be confirmed and the plan corrected first. Only package 1 (CustomersController) has a detailed spec, and right now Fable can only do two pieces of it without guessing. The first is a cut-down S1: task T1.1-01, which makes partner/client return the BP number instead of the whole Client. The second is S2: adding ConfigureAwait and preparing test kits. I re-checked their preconditions on 2026-10-02. ServicioSAP is at HEAD 2cf425f with only the 4 credit files modified (+109/-64), BusinessPartnerController.cs:48 still reads 'return Ok(result);' and BusinessPartnerMethods.cs:578 still has Fiscalregimen "". Even that first session needs these prompt fixes:
- The root path in SKILL.md (CATECINF214058D) cannot be reached from this machine, and the rules tell Fable to stop on a bad path.
- GUIA §9b builds from a Z: drive that does not exist.
- You need to decide whether Fable updates Business Rules Ecommerce.md: SKILL.md:29 requires it, while 01_CustomersController.md:86 forbids it.
- T1.1-02 (FiscalRegimen 605) should wait for an answer from the SAP fiscal owner.

For the other packages:
- Packages 2-9 have open business decisions and no detailed spec. I list 116 rules to confirm, in your WHAT / LAN WHERE / SAP WHERE / EXAMPLE / OPTIONS / RECOMMENDATION format.
- Packages 10-14 have no code work for Fable; they only need scope confirmations.
- The credit tasks R1/R3/R4/T1a are settled as business rules, but the diff baseline they check is stale: CREDITO says +126/-44, ACTIVIDADES says +161/-64, and the code is +109/-64. Every line they cite has moved, and R4 step 2 as written would undo DU13 (first name plus middle name), so Fable would stop at step 1.

I did not edit, build, run SQL or call any endpoint.

rules_to_confirm.what: Who updates 'Business Rules Ecommerce.md' after each Fable code change in ServicioSAP.
rules_to_confirm.lan_where: N/A: this is a process rule. The conflict is between documents. SKILL.md:29 (2026-10-01) requires the update. 01_CustomersController.md:86 forbids editing other vault docs without approval. PLAN_FABLE_POR_CONTROLADOR.md:56-70 (mandatory reading and closure criteria) never mentions Business Rules.
rules_to_confirm.sap_where: SKILL.md:29: the route block and its file:line citations are updated in the same change, and 'un cambio de código sin esa actualización no está terminado'. The S1-S5 'Al terminar' steps (01:1114, :1142, :1171, :1199, :1226) leave it out. The block S1 affects is Business Rules Ecommerce.md:1652-1690 (POST /partner/client; its 'Salida y errores' section says 200 with the full Client), plus the pending items at :4387.
rules_to_confirm.example: After T1.1-01, Business Rules still says partner/client returns the Client. Under SKILL.md:29 the session is not finished, but under 01:86 Fable may not correct the document.
options: A: Authorize Fable to update only the affected route blocks and their citations, never reusing rule ids, and add this as an 'Al terminar' step in every session prompt
B: The user updates Business Rules after each session
C: Leave it out (SKILL.md:29 is then not met)
rules_to_confirm.recommendation: A. Add it to PLAN_FABLE:56-70 and to every spec prompt.

rules_to_confirm.what: HTTP status and body policy for failure branches: 'always 200 with the business result in the body' versus each route's LAN contract.
rules_to_confirm.lan_where: It differs by route. LAN Controllers/CustomersController.cs:15-21 has no try, so failures become 500 and the DMZ answers BadRequest (DMZ CustomersController.cs:34-35). LAN OrdersController.cs:139-161 always answers 200 with a literal. LAN Metodos/CustomerServiceMethods.cs:1250-1254 rethrows, giving 500.
rules_to_confirm.sap_where: GUIA_MIGRACION_FABLE.md:166-170 (§1.5, marked verified) says ServicioSAP always answers HTTP 200. PLAN_FABLE_POR_CONTROLADOR.md:66 adds 'con HTTP 200' as a closure criterion. Business Rules Ecommerce.md documents routes that answer 400/404/500 today (e.g. :703, :781, :1298, :3340). DMZ Helper/Curl.cs:130-146 turns a ServicioSAP 4xx/5xx into a 200 text body. Magento decides retries from the status code (Omnipro/PlaceOrder/Model/OrderManagement.php:596-610; Omnipro/RmaIntegration/Model/RmaManagement.php:174-176).
rules_to_confirm.example: setCustomer with a BP01 error: on the LAN path Magento got 400 with an empty body; on the ServicioSAP path it gets 200 'WebException ... Body: ...'. setOrder with no stock: 200, Magento marks the order synced and never retries it.
options: A: Per route, match LAN's status and body, overriding GUIA §1.5 where LAN differed
B: Keep GUIA §1.5 (always 200) and accept that Magento loses its retry signals
C: Decide route by route (CQ6, R7a-1, R7b-4, R8-02, R8-03, R9-07), with A as the default
rules_to_confirm.recommendation: C, defaulting to A. Fable must never change an existing ServicioSAP or DMZ status code unless that route's rule says to. Correct GUIA §1.5 and PLAN:66 to match.

rules_to_confirm.what: Hard-coded OData service paths versus SKILL rule 20 ('never hard-coded, they go in Web.config') for new ServicioSAP code.

rules_to_confirm.sap_where: SKILL.md:60 (rule 20) forbids inline service paths. C: Centralize together with P14-1

rules_to_confirm.what: customer/setCustomer → partner/client: which request field fills BP NameFirst, NameLast and NameLst2, and whether names and SmtpAddr are uppercased. Also: what Magento really sends in name/lastName/lastName2/gender/storeCode/idMagento, and who reads the returned account.
rules_to_confirm.lan_where: LAN Metodos/CustomerMethods.cs:21-23 (the comments say name = apellido paterno, lastName = apellido materno, lastName2 = nombre(s)) and :75-77. SP_eCommerceCtenuevo.sql:45 and :115-118 write Cte.Nombre = UPPER(Apaterno Amaterno Nombres), with PersonalApellidoPaterno = UPPER(name), PersonalApellidoMaterno = UPPER(lastName) and PersonalNombres = UPPER(lastName2). Line :133 sets eMail1 = UPPER(email). Sexo = UPPER(gender) (:132).
rules_to_confirm.sap_where: ServicioSAP BusinessPartnerMethods.cs:422-424 and :477-479 set NameFirst = name, NameLast = lastName and NameLst2 = lastName2, trimmed only. SmtpAddr = email unchanged (:427, :514). Gender = MapGender (:482, :777-798; empty becomes '1' since 2026-09-26). Business Rules RBP-5, RBP-9, RBP-14 (:1666, :1670, :1675). No caller exists in Magento248/app/code.
rules_to_confirm.example:
Payload {name:'Ana', lastName:'Lopez', lastName2:'Ruiz', email:'ana@example.invalid', gender:'M'}.
- LAN: PersonalApellidoPaterno=ANA, PersonalNombres=RUIZ, eMail1=ANA@EXAMPLE.INVALID.
- ServicioSAP: NameFirst=Ana, NameLst2=Ruiz, SmtpAddr unchanged, Gender=2 (female).
- Credit later builds 'nombre' from NameFirst (DU13): 'Ana' in SAP against 'RUIZ' in LAN.
options: A: Strict parity: NameLast=UPPER(name), NameLst2=UPPER(lastName), NameFirst=UPPER(lastName2), SmtpAddr=UPPER(email)
B: Keep the current field mapping and only uppercase the names and email
C: No change; record it as an accepted difference
rules_to_confirm.recommendation: First capture one real, anonymized Magento payload. If name is the first name, as every vault test assumes, choose B: uppercasing follows the DU12 principle ('si LAN usa mayúsculas se replica'), and the field swap is recorded as an accepted difference. Choose A only if Magento really sends the paternal surname in name. Use the same capture to check gender: 'M' currently maps to female.
rules_to_confirm.who_decides: User, with the Magento/Omnipro team (payload and response consumer)

rules_to_confirm.what: customer/setCustomer: when a BP already exists for this idMagento, return it, update it or create a new one? And which one to use when several BPs share a ZidMagento?
rules_to_confirm.lan_where: SP_eCommerceCtenuevo.sql:62-68 searches Cte by (IdMagento AND eMail1) OR (IdMagento AND Id>2). With no ORDER BY, the last row read wins. Lines :172-201 update the existing row, and also blank the address with CP 0 (:181-187). Line :205 returns the same account.
rules_to_confirm.sap_where: Missing. ServicioSAP BusinessPartnerMethods.cs:465 always sends Partner = '', so BP01 creates a new BP on every call (RBP-21, Business Rules :1682). A lookup is possible with GetFilterClientsAsync (:249-291). A partial update through the Client model would send the non-nullable bools and ints as false/0, including Xblck, Loevm and ZidMagento (RBP-24, :1704).
rules_to_confirm.example: setCustomer posted twice with idMagento 10555: LAN returns the same C account both times, while ServicioSAP creates 2 BPs. Orders and credit later find 2 BPs with ZidMagento 10555.
options: a: Look up and return the existing Partner, with no update
b: Look up and update names and email through a new partial-update DTO (new member, needs approval)
c: Replicate the SP update, including the address wipe
d: Keep creating a new BP each time and record the difference
rules_to_confirm.recommendation: a, with a deterministic tie-break such as the highest Partner, written down. b only once a partial DTO built from RSG/bp01_bp02_maestro.md is approved. Never c. This depends on step 0 proving that BP05 filters by an unquoted ZidMagento.

rules_to_confirm.what: customer/setCustomer with an invalid idMagento or storeCode, and the 'mavi' store.

Keep the tolerant behavior

reviews.summary:
No. The per-controller plan is not ready to run with Fable for packages 2-6 (Prospecto, Wholesale, Wallet, Status, Recommender). Business rules have to be confirmed first, and then a detailed spec has to be written for each package in the format of 01_CustomersController.md. Only package 1 has such a spec; packages 2-6 have 3-9 lines each in PLAN_FABLE_POR_CONTROLADOR.md.

The code of these 5 controllers has not changed since 2026-09-14 (DMZ last 2026-09-04, ServicioSAP last 2026-09-10). What drifted is the plan:
- The Wallet count is wrong: getMinimumCostToRedeem was bridged to ServicioSAP on 2026-09-04, so it is 2 SAP / 1 LAN, not 1 / 2.
- The Wholesale warning that the route does not exist is stale: company/wholesale-customer exists and has been bridged since 2026-08-26.
- Package 6 does not lack prior analysis: there are 5 mapping docs.
- Status and Recommender are still listed although other docs dropped them (Status on 2026-08-11; Recommender is marked DEPRECADO in the tracker, and setRecommenderList was dropped on 2026-08-31).
- Package 2 is not 'contained, no external dependencies': prospecto/rfc needs 4 Intelisis tables (RFCAnexoI-IV) that have no destination.

There are 17 open decisions, each written up with WHAT, LAN WHERE, SAP WHERE, EXAMPLE, OPTIONS and RECOMMENDATION:
- Prospecto (5): where the RFC annex data comes from; validation and messages; matching on all given names (the DU13 lesson); masking (C17); permission to escape the filter (C12).
- Wholesale (3): whether Magento sends a C-account or a BP number (the DMZ now rejects C-accounts); person name vs company name; the full SAP design of negotiable-quote (ZMAY org, channel, plant, agent, payment term, review block, or retire it).
- Wallet (7): what 'Wallet' means as a destination; UEN handling (C10); titular; the SD18 lookup key; the generate-wallet side effect; the C09 algorithm with catalog and status semantics; retire getCuentaC.
- Status (1): in scope or not, and what 'healthy' means.
- Recommender (1): confirm it is deprecated.

Statuses: packages 2-5 are NEEDS_SPEC_FIRST. Package 6 is OUT_OF_SCOPE pending your confirmation.

Suggested order:
1. Decide scope for Status, Recommender and getCuentaC. The evidence points to retiring all three.
2. Answer the global C-account vs BP question.
3. Answer the per-package questions.
4. Write specs 02-04 with Fable, which in the meantime can do read-only evidence work where SAP QA is reachable: captures of BP05, SD18, DM01 and the AWS catalogs. Prospecto is the best calibration case once P2-Q1 to P2-Q5 are answered.
5. Fix the code baseline (commit or stash the uncommitted credit edits, and rebuild the DLL) before any E2E.

The DMZ has 19 active routes: 4 already go to ServicioSAP (setOrder, getGuide, cancelOrder, returnOrder), 8 still go to LAN and 7 go directly to Magento. A 20th route, validateCredit, is commented out. The sub-package table also mixes in five LAN-only routes the DMZ does not expose, and leaves out ManagePaynetOrders, GetPickUpCode, getGuide and authorizationResult.

Readiness by sub-package:
- **7a (order creation):** ready only after about 10 confirmations. Fable could start once they are answered and a spec is written. The guest BP and the generic agent are data MAVI still has to deliver; the code already uses placeholders, so they do not stop Fable. The División value stays fixed at "01", so it is not a Fable blocker.
- **7b (cancel and return):** returnOrder (order/setreturn) and the cancel input fix can be done after 8 confirmations. The main cancel case, an order that has no delivery yet, is blocked until the SAP team provides the API that marks an order as annulled (ZIDSTATUS=03). The policy for cancelling an already-invoiced order is an open business decision.
- **7c (credit routes):** blocked by other teams. The validator (liberador) is owned by Valentín. creditStatus and updateCreditOrderId need decisions from the credit area, Alan and Dev 2, plus a new SAP service (OData) for ZIdEcommerce. These routes are handled in the credit plan, not here. validateCredit is not applicable.
- **7d (Openpay and pickup):** needs a spec first. Nothing reprocesses Openpay card orders in ServicioSAP, so those orders never reach SAP. Several pieces are undefined: who triggers checkOpenpay, a bypass parameter equivalent to LAN's `liberado` flag, the Openpay SDK and keys, where the rejection statuses come from, where InsertPaymentData should write, what replaces "AFECTAR" for Paynet orders, and who calls createStorepickupCode.
- **7e (queries):** needs a spec first. getPosCancellations is mapped to the opposite operation (cancelInvoice). SD36 cannot list cancelled orders by date. There is no SAP source for the estimated-delivery tracking data. getIntelisisStatuses needs a mapping to the CONCLUIDO/CANCELADO values Magento expects. The decisions to retire getOrderId (P9) and getOrderInfoAndSet (P11) are not confirmed.

Reading the code and Magento248 turned up four defects that are not in the plan:
1. **Every Magento cancellation comes back "noexiste".** Magento sends `tipo` "T"/"P" (total/partial), and ServicioSAP builds the SAP order key from it as ZSD_T_… instead of ZSD_ZMER_…, so the order is never found.
2. **Every Magento return fails silently.** Magento's return body has no `store`, so order/setreturn throws "No lleva id de tienda". The DMZ still answers 200, so Magento marks the return as synced.
3. **Failed orders are never retried.** setOrder errors (no stock, "Error, …", ServicioSAP unreachable) all reach Magento as 200. Magento marks them synced and its retry cron skips them.
4. **Magento never stores the account.** Magento expects the setOrder body to be a bare 10-digit BP before it records the account, but the DMZ now returns a JSON object.

HTTP 200 for every outcome hides failures from Magento. rules_to_confirm.what: setOrder response to Magento: HTTP status and body for success, PedidoExistente and errors (Resultado 'Error', 'Error, …' string, ServicioSAP unreachable).
rules_to_confirm.lan_where: LAN-OC:139-161 always returns 200: the account 'C…' or a literal (LOM:732), and on exception Ok(e.ToString()). The pre-migration DMZ (commit c63c0ab, setOrder) mapped PrecioIncorrecto/Incorrecto→400, ''→500, PedidoExistente→409, 'sin cuenta'→422, not starting with 'C'→500, success→200 with the bare account. Magento OrderManagement.php:596-610: setCAccount runs only if the body is a 10-character BP; 200/100 → synced=1; otherwise the cron Registry retries.
rules_to_confirm.sap_where: SS-OC:16-48 returns 200 with {BP, SalesDocument, Message, Resultado} or 200 with 'Error, …'. Duplicates: OM:1741-1749. DMZ-OC:214-227 passes through with 200. DMZ-CURL:130-146 turns errors into text.
rules_to_confirm.example: The Magento cron re-sends 2000012345 with forzarOrder '0'. Before: 409, synced stays 0, retried. Now: 200 {"BP":null,"SalesDocument":null,"Message":"","Resultado":"PedidoExistente"}, synced=1. The same 200 comes back when DIM11 has no stock or ServicioSAP is down, so the paid order is marked synced and never retried. Magento's local setCAccount never runs because the body is JSON.
options: A) Keep 200 plus the object (GUIA §1.5, P12-A). Accept that errors are not retried. Rely on ServicioSAP's setCAccount callback (RORD-36, OM:1930-1934)
B) Restore the legacy DMZ status mapping (409/422/500). This goes against GUIA §1.5
C) ServicioSAP returns LAN's body (bare BP on success, literal on PedidoExistente) with 200; DMZ unchanged
D) Magento change: read Resultado/BP from the JSON and keep synced=0 when Resultado is 'Error'
rules_to_confirm.recommendation: A for PedidoExistente: 200 is what LAN itself returned, and it ends the retry loop. Decide separately, with the Magento owner, how failed orders get retried (D is the lowest-risk option). Fable must not touch DMZ status codes.

reviews.summary:
No. Packages 8 (CustomerServiceController) and 9 (CreditController, without the credit-order work) are not ready to hand to Fable 5.1 as the plan is written. Business rules need confirming first, and each package needs a detailed spec like 01_CustomersController.md. Today the plan has only one paragraph for each (PLAN_FABLE_POR_CONTROLADOR.md:152-172), and several of its premises are wrong or out of date.

Main facts, checked against the code on 2026-10-02:
(1) The 8a 'quick wins' premise is false.
- The two Login routes are already switched to PostSAP on the DMZ branch ConexionSAP (commit 212b04e, 2026-09-01). They are not contract-equal with LAN. There are 5 open differences: email source, error turned into 200 false, 400 on empty input, lenient date parsing plus a bug for births before 1970, and how the name is built.
- GetEmpleadoByNomina has no destination in ServicioSAP. The candidate partner/successfactor/employee/{userId} is an internal wrapper that returns raw SuccessFactors rows. The real consumer (Magento RegisterSeller) reads Nombre and Nomina, so switching the DMZ there would break it.
(2) 8b (BBVA/STP) is blocked. There is no SAP write target for the payment intents and confirmations that LAN keeps in CXCCFacturaMultipagoBBVA. ZAPI_REFERENCIAS_BANCARIAS and ZFICRUD_COBREF_SRV have no RSG fiche, and the ABAP logic is missing. It belongs to Dev 4. The Neko stubs are CustomerServiceController routes (the plan puts them in package 9). Magento still has the Neko module enabled.
(3) 8c: obtenerCreditos was already built in ServicioSAP by Dev 2 on 2026-09-15, outside the plan. It has differences: 3 statuses instead of 5, uen ignored, different id, no sorting or rounding, discount fixed at 0. The DMZ still routes it to LAN. nombreCliente, validarCoberturaPorCP and obtenerVentanaConfirmacion need equivalences that no one has documented. ObtenerEstatusEmbarque is still blocked by ABAP.
(4) 8 of the 26 routes are not in any of 8a, 8b or 8c.
- 5 are already bridged. GetAccountDebts among them is broken (C08), and validarCliente has two regressions.
- 3 Tablerate routes point to LAN routes that were removed in 2022.
- obtenerTipoGarantia and bitacoraAtencionClientes are planned by Dev 3.
(5) Package 9:
- Six routes are already bridged. SendSmsNewNumber, guardardocumento and SaveImagesProductosMx have E2E evidence (E-01, E-07, E-08); getPlazos is done except its error branch. getClienteFactura always returns 500, because ServicioSAP returns an array and the DMZ parses an object. GetCreditAmounts returns 500 until someone fills mavi_credilana_info (still no owner).
- getSms and validateSms exist in ServicioSAP and their response codes match LAN. The only work left is switching the DMZ, which waits on cutover timing and on porting GetPhoneValidatedClientSecretName (SPEC_NIP_SMS §5.1).
- The saldo source is now broken down into N1-N16 with owners (getClienteSaldo analysis, 2026-10-01).
- 12 routes need a scope decision: Credilana (only CreditoWeb_Seguro is confirmed out; SPCREDICredilana is also called by CreditoWeb_Informacion, CreditoWeb_Solicitud and CreditoWeb_SolicitudPrimerGuardado), deprecated, or APP mercancías (SolicitudMercancia).
(6) Ownership overlaps with the Dev 2, Dev 3 and Dev 4 checklists.
(7) The plan's own order says packages 1-3 come first, and package 1 still has 17 open decisions.

Only two slices are close to ready:
- The DMZ switch of getSms/validateSms, after R9-01 and R9-02.
- Parity fixes on the two already-bridged Login routes, after R8-01 to R8-05.
